mechanism_narrative: A sustained federal funds rate below 0.25% indicates accommodative monetary policy that compresses equity discount rates, generating positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS remains below 0.25%.

mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate rise above 0.25% signals imminent monetary tightening, increasing equity discount rates and causing negative S&P 500 returns within 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS crosses above 0.25%.

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent decline in unemployment rate and rise in payroll employment signal strengthening labor market conditions, boosting consumer spending and corporate earnings growth for positive S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: The joint signal of falling UNRATE and rising PAYEMS fails to produce positive 60-day SPX returns in more than 60% of instances.

mechanism_narrative: Housing starts exceeding 550,000 units during post-recession housing recovery phases indicate robust residential demand, driving positive S&P 500 returns over 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when HOUST exceeds 550 and the regime is post-recession housing recovery.

mechanism_narrative: Rising payroll employment (PAYEMS) indicates expanding labor market conditions that support consumer spending and corporate growth, producing positive S&P 500 returns within 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when PAYEMS is rising.

mechanism_narrative: Unemployment rate decline below 9.0% signals improving labor market health, increasing consumer confidence and spending, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when UNRATE falls below 9.0%.

mechanism_narrative: Joint increases in industrial production and housing starts indicate strong supply capacity and demand for goods, driving economic expansion and positive S&P 500 returns over 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint signal of rising INDPRO and rising HOUST fails to produce positive 20-day SPX returns in more than 60% of instances.

mechanism_narrative: Industrial production decline below 95 during supply shock regimes signals reduced economic output, increasing recession risks and causing negative S&P 500 returns within 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when INDPRO falls below 95 and the regime is supply shock.
